newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended lower following U.S. Treasuries after Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan Greenspan said he cannot rule out tighter monetary policy.
But bonos recovered some losses by the end of the day which dealers saw as a sign of strength.
"We were hit by Greenspan's words as were other markets, but later both the peseta and bonos proved to be resilient with good buying interest on every dip," a dealer in Madrid said.
The 10-year spread over Bunds ended around 118 basis point, a bit lower than Tuesday's close of 120 basis points.
The peseta, which began the day with a very weak tone ended a bit higher.
"We had an improvement, though slight, which is important," another dealer in Madrid said.
The yield curve remained virtually unchanged.
The yield on six-month bills auctioned in the morning rose to 5.315 percent from 5.172 percent two weeks ago.
